clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old female undergoing annual mammographic screening was found to have many enlarged axillary lymph nodes bilaterally with no suspicious breast findings. She had no breast or axillary symptoms and no recent vaccinations. She had known autoimmune diseases including mixed connective tissue disease and psoriatic arthropathy. Previous screening in 2017 showed no axillary adenopathy. Although physical exam findings, laboratory inflammatory markers, and biopsy results were not documented, the diagnosis was supported by the known autoimmune conditions and the absence of infectious or neoplastic symptoms, consistent with an inflammatory etiology of the lymphadenopathies.
